description:
## Goal
Make fz read source the way Elixir does: ONE uniform read in which a
def-head (fn/fnp/defmacro/defmodule/defprotocol/defimpl) is just a call —
specifically a macro call — and let the *structure* of a definition emerge
from the expand -> Fz.Compiler.define -> define pipeline, not from a second,
mode-gated structural re-parse of the source. The deliverable is the deletion
of ScopeSurfaceMode and of the read-time typed-form parse of def-heads.

## Why this exists (corrected from fz-hwn.19.2.4.17)
.17 claimed the def-head "macro bounce" was a no-op identity round-trip and
proposed deleting it. That premise is wrong. The bounce is load-bearing and
Elixir-aligned:

- runtime.fz:40-58 — each def-head macro wraps the node in
  `Fz.Compiler.define(unquote(source), unquote(__CALLER__))`, capturing the
  lexical environment.
- Elixir does the same: defmodule (kernel.ex:5163), def (5382),
  defprotocol (5732), defimpl (5743) are all Kernel macros that capture
  __CALLER__/__ENV__ and emit a compiler-internal call
  (`:elixir_module.compile(..., __ENV__)`).

So the bounce STAYS. The real divergence — the thing ScopeSurfaceMode is a
symptom of — is that fz *additionally* parses def-heads into typed ScopeForms
(Module/Function/Protocol/ProtocolImpl) at read time, a step Elixir has no
equivalent of. In Elixir, a def-head's name/arity/clauses/body are extracted
during expansion and module compilation (`:elixir_def.store_definition`,
`:elixir_module.compile`), never by a source-surface parser.

## The divergence, precisely
`build_form` (quoted_surface.rs:331-374) inspects `mode` in exactly ONE place
(:354): in Source mode a scope-definition head becomes a `MacroCall`; in
CompilerFragment mode the same head is parsed directly into a typed form
(parse_function_form / parse_module_form / parse_protocol_form /
parse_protocol_impl_form). The enum is threaded purely to reach that one branch
through read_scope_surface_with_mode, read_do_body_surface_with_mode, and
flush_function_groups.

Two readers, two jobs, one moded function:
- read_scope_surface (Source, :167) — reads USER source; def-head -> MacroCall.
- read_compiler_fragment_surface (CompilerFragment, :174) — reads the
  POST-EXPANSION inner node `{:defmodule|...}` that Fz.Compiler.define carries
  (apply_compiler_define, source_publish.rs:643-691), plus protocol/impl bodies
  and discovery re-reads, into typed forms.

There is already a THIRD, lighter def-head recognizer:
`reserved_source_definition` (quoted_surface.rs:710-762) extracts only the
reserved name/arity from a def-head MacroCall, used to seed the namespace
before any macro runs (source_publish.rs reserve/discover paths). That
lightweight name recognition IS the Elixir-compatible minimum an incremental
compiler legitimately needs (fz is not a linear compiler; it must surface
definition names out of order). The full typed re-parse is the part that is
not.

## Strategy (work backwards from "ScopeSurfaceMode is deleted")
1. Source reads in one mode. Def-heads are MacroCalls, uniformly. No
   CompilerFragment variant of the *source* reader.
2. Incremental name discovery stays on the lightweight reserved_source_definition
   recognizer (name/arity only) — the Elixir-compatible seed.
3. The full structural extraction of a def-head (function clauses/specs/arity;
   module name+body; protocol/impl shape) moves INTO the expand/define pipeline
   where Fz.Compiler.define already lands with __CALLER__ in hand — the analogue
   of store_definition / module compile — rather than being produced by a
   mode-switched source reader. Establish exactly which consumers
   (apply_compiler_define, read_protocol_body_surface,
   read_protocol_impl_body_surface, discover_modules, register_protocol_impl_*)
   need a typed form and feed them from the define tier, not from a moded read.
4. Delete ScopeSurfaceMode and the CompilerFragment branch of build_form once no
   consumer reads a typed def-head form from the source reader.

## What goes away
- enum ScopeSurfaceMode (quoted_surface.rs:34-38) and the `mode` parameter on
  read_scope_surface_with_mode, read_do_body_surface_with_mode,
  flush_function_groups, build_form.
- read_compiler_fragment_surface / read_compiler_fragment_root as a *source*
  reader of def-heads (its structural job relocates into the define pipeline).
- The CompilerFragment match arm in build_form (:359-365).

## Open questions to resolve before decomposition (no hidden surprises)
- Does any def-head structural parse need lexical context the define tier lacks
  at the point it currently runs? (function_env / project_env_value already
  threads __ENV__; confirm parity.)
- discover_modules currently has BOTH direct typed arms and MacroCall+fragment
  re-read arms — which fire, and can the typed arms be served by the reserved
  recognizer + define-tier extraction alone?
- Protocol / protocol-impl bodies are read in CompilerFragment today; map their
  structural needs onto the new single-read model.

## Tests / signal
Behavior must be invariant: full lib suite green (no regressions), clippy clean.
Add telemetry/assertions that a def-head is read exactly once as a MacroCall and
its typed structure is produced by the define tier (observe the existing
macro-expanded / Fz.Compiler.define events rather than a second source read).

## References
- elixir/lib/elixir/lib/kernel.ex:5163,5382,5732,5743 (Kernel def-head macros)
- src/modules/runtime_library/runtime.fz:40-58 (fz def-head macros)
- src/compiler2/quoted_surface.rs:34-38,163-175,331-374,710-762
- src/compiler2/source_publish.rs:643-691 (apply_compiler_define),
  740-748 (apply_item_macro_call), 750-772 (apply_surface_fragment)
- src/compiler2/quoted_expander.rs:174-176,467-513,535-628

comments.text: Adopted as the phase-vs-origin step of epic fz-rh2.28 (replaces the deleted fz-rh2.28.2). Reconciliation with the rest of the epic: (1) fz-rh2.28.1 names the bootstrap boundary first, so this ticket can route bootstrap-direct vs user-bounce cleanly; the bootstrap is the lone code whose def-heads cannot be MacroCalls (the macros are defined in it), so its def-heads reach the define tier DIRECTLY via the reserved_source_definition recognizer plus define-tier extraction, with no macro bounce. (2) fz-rh2.28.3 (carry the definition env) attaches env at the same define-tier seam where this ticket relocates structural extraction; user defs carry __CALLER__ via Fz.Compiler.define, bootstrap defs project env at the define tier. The two tickets touch one seam; do this one first (chain: .1 -> fz-s00 -> .3).

title: fz/Elixir alignment: read source once; def-head structure emerges from the define pipeline, not a mode-gated re-parse
